summary: GuideStar Israel identifies ECF as amuta 580187078, founded in 1991, but exposes no 1991-1993 financial or donor filings.
detail: The public registrar record gives the Hebrew and English legal names, amuta number 580187078, founding year 1991, and statutory economic-cooperation purposes. Its current public document horizon begins much later: named donations in 2012, annual reports in 2017, and finance series data in 2018. The founders call returned an empty list and officers were CAPTCHA-gated. Consequently the public registrar layer cannot provide an account-complete year-one/year-two funder roster.

summary: A European Commission research contract supported an ECF-associated Hirschfeld study dated September 1992.
detail: Sven Behrendt's academic account says Hirschfeld produced Israel, the Palestinians and the Middle East: From Dependency to Interdependence under a research contract from the EC Commission and associates the Commission with ECF. Hirschfeld later dated the report to September 1992. This names a supranational European public funder in ECF's second year, but the accessible sources do not disclose the amount, award date, or recipient account.
source_quote: im Rahmen eines Forschungsauftrags der EG-Kommission

target_name: Economic Cooperation Foundation / Friedrich Ebert Stiftung
summary: FES's ECF collaboration began with a September 1991 presentation and included financial support for Hirschfeld and Pundak's 1993 Oslo activity.
detail: FES's institutional history says Beilin and Hirschfeld presented the newly founded ECF at FES headquarters in Bonn in September 1991, marking the beginning of their collaboration. It later says Hirschfeld and Pundak went to Oslo with financial support from FES and cites 1993 support for seminars in Brussels and Washington. FES is a named early German institutional supporter; the source does not give an amount, grant number, payment date, or ECF ledger receipt.
source_quote: unter anderem auch mit finanzieller Unterstützung der FES

target_name: Economic Cooperation Foundation / European development agencies
summary: A scholarly account attributes ECF's 1991 establishment to financing from plural European development agencies.
detail: Anthony Wanis-St. John writes that Beilin and Hirschfeld set up ECF in 1991 with financing from European development agencies and that ECF employed Hirschfeld and Ron Pundak full time. The source establishes a collective European institutional funding category but does not name every agency, provide amounts, or demonstrate the recipient accounts. The European Commission and FES are separately evidenced named members of the early support map, but the plural category may include additional unidentified funders.
source_quote: Beilin and Hirschfeld, with the financing of European development agencies, set up an NGO called the Economic Cooperation Foundation (ECF) in 1991

target_name: Economic Cooperation Foundation principals / Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
summary: The earliest documented Norwegian MFA commitment to finance the pre-official channel is 1992-09-09; Fafo payroll and logistics were operating by January 1993.
detail: Waage reports that State Secretary Jan Egeland said on 1992-09-09 that the Norwegian MFA stood behind Fafo and would finance a back-channel project. Hirschfeld and Pundak were then put on Fafo's payroll, and Norwegian support covered the first January 1993 round and channel logistics. This is Norwegian public financing of the channel and ECF personnel through Fafo, not proof of a direct grant into ECF's account.
source_quote: the Norwegian foreign ministry was behind Fafo and would back and finance a back channel project

target_name: Economic Cooperation Foundation / Government of Norway
summary: GuideStar's current donation series first shows a named direct Norwegian government donation to ECF in 2013 for NIS 118,900.
detail: The public named-donation series contains no Norwegian donor in 2012 and lists Government of Norway in 2013 at NIS 118,900 for improving life in the territories. Because online donation records begin in 2012, this is the earliest visible named direct Norwegian donation, not proof that 2013 was Norway's first actual ECF payment.

target_name: Economic Cooperation Foundation / American private donors
summary: No American private donor to ECF in 1991-1993 was verified across the available registrar, institutional, participant, academic, foundation-report, archive-index, press-index, and local-corpus layers.
detail: Ford Foundation's official 1991, 1992, and 1993 annual reports each returned zero hits for six ECF/person-name variants. Exact English and Hebrew ECF searches returned 0 hits in each of five local source tools; the Hirschfeld-Pundak pair returned 4/1/4/0/0 records, all general Oslo narratives with zero funding rosters. GuideStar exposes zero 1991-1993 financial or donor filings; its series begin in 2012 or later. The earliest Wayback capture was 2000-03-01 with zero substantive funding content. JPress-domain exact Hebrew index searches returned zero useful contemporaneous results, and current ECF pages name no 1991-1993 American donor. This bounded null does not exclude anonymous, intermediary, unfiled, or OCR-missed payments, but pre-committed rule 4 is not triggered on the evidence found.
